This species of Garra was obtained for the first time. In this genus it is currently impossible to guarantee the exact determination of the species, as a huge number of species have been described and most of them look extremely similar to each other. The fish are at least very close to G. vittatula.

Maximum size reported for Garra vittatula in scientific literature is about 6-8 cm, so the specimens are probably fully grown already.

There is one very obvious behaviour in G. vittatula: it is extremely social. The specimens regularly search for conspecifics. So this species should be kept in small schools composed of at least 5 specimens.

All species of Garra are good algae eaters and are usually kept for that purpose rather than for their coloration. However, well established G. vittatula look quite attractive, maybe because they often show a reddish caudal fin.
